## Three roads to gene counts {#roads}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart TD
  T["trimmed reads"] --> G1["align to genome<br/>STAR, HISAT2"] --> G2["count on genes<br/>featureCounts"]
  T --> P1["map to transcriptome<br/>Salmon, kallisto"] --> P2["tximport"]
  G2 & P2 --> D["DESeq2"]
```

bagPipes: **Salmon** for counts, **HISAT2** for BAMs and tracks.

## Aligners {#aligners}

| Tool | Splice-aware | RAM (human) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **STAR** | yes | ~32 GB | fast, standard |
| **HISAT2** | yes | ~8 GB | bagPipes |
| TopHat | yes | | obsolete |
| Bowtie2, BWA | **no** | | DNA: ChIP, ATAC — **not RNA** |

Assume: right genome; GT–AG introns; multi-mappers get low MAPQ.

## Pseudoaligners {#pseudoaligners}

| Tool | How |
|---|---|
| **Salmon** | selective alignment + EM; bias models |
| **kallisto** | pseudoalignment on a de Bruijn graph |

Assume: **every RNA is in the annotation**. Intronic / intergenic reads have
nowhere to go → total RNA maps lower. **No genome coordinates.**

## Strandedness: many names {#strand-names}

| Tool | dUTP | unstranded | read-1-sense |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salmon `-l` | `ISR` | `IU` | `ISF` |
| featureCounts `-s` | `2` | `0` | `1` |
| HTSeq `-s` | `reverse` | `no` | `yes` |
| HISAT2 | `RF` | – | `FR` |
| STAR GeneCounts col. | 4 | 2 | 3 |

## The RNApipe map {#pipeline-map}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart TD
  R["raw FASTQ"] --> FQ["fastqc"] & TR["trim"]
  TR --> QU["quant (Salmon)"] --> TX["tximport"]
  TR --> AL["align (HISAT2)"] --> SI["signal"] & SS["strandedSignal"]
  FQ & TR & QU & AL & SI & SS --> MQ["multiqc"]
  AL -.-> MA["mergeAlign"] -.-> MS["mergeSignal"]
```

## Files in, files out {#files}

| Step | In | Out |
|---|---|---|
| FastQC | raw FASTQ | `_fastqc.html` |
| Trim Galore | raw FASTQ | `_trimmed.fastq.gz` |
| Salmon | trimmed + index | `quant.sf` |
| HISAT2 | trimmed + index | `_sorted.bam` |
| bamCoverage | BAM | `.bw` |
| tximport | all `quant.sf` + GTF | `_tximport.rds` |

FastQC files and trimmed FASTQs are `temp()`: deleted after MultiQC.

::: {.book-link}
[The RNApipe map](../rna-seq/pipeline-map.html)
:::

## FastQC: is the run OK? {#fastqc}

```bash
fastqc -o fastqc $DATA/*_001.fastq.gz
```

| Module | Worry if… |
|---|---|
| Per-base quality | collapses mid-read |
| Adapter content | high early in the read |
| GC content | sharp extra peak |
| Overrepresented | adapter / primer dimers at the top |

## Two "fails" to ignore in RNA-seq {#fastqc-ignore}

1. **Per-base sequence content**, first ~12 bases: random-hexamer bias
2. **Duplication levels**: highly expressed genes, not PCR

Compare samples: the **outlier** matters more than the flag.

::: {.book-link}
[FastQC](../rna-seq/fastqc.html)
:::

## Trimming: why {#trimming}

```
before:  GATTTGGGGTTCAAAGCAGTATCG AGATCGGAAGAGC ACACGTCTGAA
                 insert              └─ adapter ─┘
after:   GATTTGGGGTTCAAAGCAGTATCG
```

- **Adapter**: insert shorter than read
- **Low-quality 3' ends**
- Reads too short afterwards → dropped

## Trim Galore defaults {#trim-galore}

```bash
trim_galore --paired -o trim R1.fastq.gz R2.fastq.gz
```

| Default | |
|---|---|
| adapter | auto-detected (Illumina `AGATCGGAAGAGC`) |
| `-q 20` | trim 3' bases below Q20 |
| `--length 20` | drop shorter reads |
| `--paired` | **drop both mates together** |

## Reading the trimming report {#trim-report}

- **Reads with adapters**: 10–40 % common
- **Bases kept**: usually > 90 %
- **Pairs removed (too short)**: well under 5 %

Many pairs removed → adapter dimers or degraded RNA.

::: {.book-link}
[Trimming](../rna-seq/trimming.html)
:::

## Try it {#try-it}

::: {.try}
```bash
cd $WALK/work
fastqc -o fastqc $DATA/*_001.fastq.gz
for S in N61311_untrt N61311_dex N052611_untrt N052611_dex; do
  trim_galore -o trim --paired $DATA/${S}_R1_001.fastq.gz $DATA/${S}_R2_001.fastq.gz
done
```
:::

Open a FastQC report. How many pairs did trimming remove?

## Recap {#recap}

- Salmon counts, HISAT2 places, featureCounts counts BAMs
- Know your **strandedness** in every tool's language
- FastQC: look for **outliers**
- Trim adapters and bad ends; keep pairs in step
